sequences.title: Wavefunctions · returning, relating, composing
sequences.thread: A body can return without occupying the same state. A trace makes that return inspectable; projection and phase let repetition organise space; excitation and composition make several returns act together.
sequences.necessity: A specified state or coordinate, a reference for progression, and a rule relating them. Distinguish a dynamically integrated pendulum from a prescribed sine, and a moving pattern from transport of matter.
sequences.handoff: Formfinding precedes Waves on the current spine. Carry equilibrium and restoring behaviour into oscillation. Leave Waves able to distinguish a complex appearance from an unspecified process; Randomness then asks what a procedure chooses.
sequences.route: Keep the current six-room museum route for the first implementation. Unit Circle and Propagation are strong candidates for later insertion between the trace and Sine Space, after their footprints are repaired. Bernini, Cage, Sky Stairs and TrigWalkingPath remain independently developed extension rooms. Recheck transitions against the route actually shipped.

sequences.title: Randomness · choosing, accumulating, excluding
sequences.thread: A reproducible procedure supplies choices; an eligibility rule and distribution decide their possibilities; accumulated choices form paths and populations; feedback and uncertain timing alter what a body can do.
sequences.necessity: A defined outcome space and selection procedure. Seed/state, draw order, distribution, boundary and interpretation are different decisions. A histogram cannot recover the order it discarded.
sequences.handoff: The five-harmonic sum is repeatable without looking simple. Start here by replaying an irregular-looking field. Finish with a body planning around random waits; Noise asks how neighbouring samples can be related.
sequences.route: Keep the seven active halls while improving all fourteen authored maps. The extension rooms supply concrete routes into estimation, feedback and correlation; they are not automatically extra museum halls. In particular Random_Space_Geometry and Random_Space overlap the next sequence: use them as comparison laboratories, not duplicate introductory lectures.

sequences.title: Noise · neighbouring, sampling, inhabiting
sequences.thread: A spatial relation constrains variation. A field becomes colour, relief, occupied volume or a route through distinct reading rules. Layers and coordinate warps expand what those fields can do; fair comparisons reveal which change actually mattered.
sequences.necessity: A sampling domain and coordinates, a field-generating rule, and a mapping from values into an appearance or consequence. Correlation alone supplies no stored history, collision, ecology or intention.
sequences.handoff: Contrast a new random draw with revisiting a coordinate in a fixed field. The current next chapter is Cellular Automata: a field supplies related values; an automaton maintains state and updates it through a neighbourhood rule. Do not promise a return to Lab_Path on the main route unless navigation is deliberately changed.
sequences.route: Keep six active halls. Repair the Perlin/Simplex claim first. Develop domain warping and walkable noise as extension rooms; decide later whether they earn main-route slots. Lab_Path is a short optional reflective exit, not another long noise lesson.

maps.body: A suspended body; the player's releasing hand.

Preserve this contract; see recovery.html and the dated doc/space archive.

Start with one release experiment. Offer a deliberate reveal of angle and signed angular velocity, using the existing evidence modes where suitable. If a damping comparison is added, change only that setting; do not introduce every regime at once.

Check the initial cube collection against old map structure before consolidating. Preserve meaningful stationary/prescribed-motion examples so a calculated pendulum is distinguishable from a cube following sin(time).
book: Open with two visits to the centre that travel in opposite directions; invite a release before explaining.
Describe position, direction and turning points, then connect the short integration excerpt to the force work already learned.
Let a second release trouble a prediction. Avoid promising exact small-angle behaviour at large releases.
End with the need to keep a record: the next room gives elapsed history a spatial direction.

maps.body: A sampled volume, a threshold and a receiving terrain.

If Fable retains two different fields, label this explicitly as shared controls and include a truly matched small comparison so the room still demonstrates the classification rule.

maps.question: Which layer of a surface are you attending to?
maps.body: An interior lined with a sum of spatial scales.
maps.findings: The room controller already supports basis choices and frozen/live modes. The shaders combine six scales; colour, density and time also move. Existing final proposes octave isolation but the visitor cannot currently perform it.
build: Keep the immersive interior, but give the entrance a stable, readable sample panel. Compare 1, 2, 4 and 6 layers under fixed seed/coordinates, contrast, colour and time.
Add an actual octave control or contribution views to the shader, reusing frozen mode. Keep basis changes as a separate comparison; do not conflate six walls with six isolated octaves.
Stage the room within the museum with a clear entrance/exit and an unobstructed margin. Use bounded shader cost and prevent material instances from changing other halls.
book: Choose a broad patch, then find detail within it before turning to the control.
Remove layers and notice what persists.
Read the shader accumulation loop and the amplitude/frequency progression.
Ask when extra detail helps a body read a route and when it obscures it. On the current route, close toward the fair Perlin/Simplex comparison.
maps.code: noiseroom.gd: _apply_generator, _update_room_animation, apply_grid_config; WallNoiseShader.gdshader and QueerNoiseShader.gdshader accumulation and colour mapping.
evidence: One layer and six layers differ only by declared contributions in the comparison mode.
Frozen mode stops every animated term used by the comparison.
Check shader compilation/performance and both museum doorway clearances.
maps.latitude: Make the walls a desirable material interior. Keep one modest comparison surface that can disclose how the enchantment was made.
maps.reuse: R1 controlled comparison; R4 sample-to-body mapping; R8 bounded simulation.

maps.question: What happens when a field changes where another field is read?
maps.body: A sampling grid, displaced coordinates and a curved surface.
maps.findings: Outside the active route. The existing sphere directly samples value noise; it does not currently implement the domain-warp comparison named by the room. the_same_cloud contains an existing FastNoiseLite warp pair that can be inspected and reused selectively. Platform/wall recovery on 10 September: 13 interior cells restored as platforms; 8 boundary cells made explicit w. Keep museum.wall_height: 3 and existing gate-depth settings. See structure-recovery.html and doc/space/sequence-platform-recovery-2026-09-10/. Keep the added landing at (7,11) before the unchanged exit at (7,12).
build: Build a real direct-versus-warped comparison using the same base field, seed, coordinates, support and material. Warp strength zero must reproduce the direct output.
Reveal several original sample locations and their displaced locations with optional connecting marks. Vary warp strength while other values remain fixed.

Keep the sphere if it makes the displacement relation visible, or use a plane first and the sphere as a secondary application. Share the actual sampling rule; do not simulate warping by changing the seed or moving the mesh alone.
book: Notice a familiar patch drawn into another arrangement and ask what moved.
Return warp strength to zero before explaining.
Show the actual implementation of sampling at displaced coordinates, with vector-valued displacement if used; distinguish this from post-sampling height displacement.
Let an ambiguous image require the coordinate witness. Close toward terrain mapping in this optional extension path.
maps.code: noisesphere.gd/noisePlanet2.gdshader for the baseline; commons/artifacts/the_same_cloud/the_same_cloud.gd: _build_warp_pair for a reuse candidate. Trace its actual FastNoiseLite settings before adapting.
evidence: At zero warp, compare field values with the direct baseline.
At a chosen point, show q=p+warp(p) and verify the output is evaluated at q.
Freeze and replay both displays without hidden colour, time or seed differences.
maps.latitude: Fable can choose a stretched skin, folded map or transformed interior. The coordinate operation is the requirement; the metaphor is open.
maps.reuse: R1 controlled comparison; R4 sample-to-body mapping; R6 local state/seed.

maps.question: Which bodies can a field carry once it becomes ground?
maps.body: A heightfield, its collider and the moving player.
maps.findings: Outside the active route. NoiseSpace samples a 2D field into one height per horizontal location and constructs a mesh with collision. The current terrain is generated at startup. Configs include basis, octave count, scale and persistence; the name does not imply ten live controls. Platform/wall recovery on 10 September: 55 interior cells restored as platforms; 40 boundary cells made explicit w. Keep museum.wall_height: 3 and existing gate-depth settings. See structure-recovery.html and doc/space/sequence-platform-recovery-2026-09-10/.
build: Recover the original ground configuration and frame it as a bounded arena with a same-level margin, intentional entry/exit and museum bypass.
Make one controlled comparison in frequency or height amplitude from a fixed seed. Rebuild mesh and collider together on deliberate changes while the player stands on the stable margin.

Offer two proposed routes or two body sizes only if they can actually be tested. Do not quietly rescale the player across the entire museum; a labelled probe body is an acceptable secondary comparison.
book: Choose a possible route from the margin, then test the path with the actual player.
Change one field-to-height parameter and revisit the route.
Read sample→height→mesh/collision, keeping the representation chain visible.
Discover the missing cave: one height cannot hold both roof and floor at the same horizontal coordinate. Link this limit to Voxel's occupied volume.
maps.code: NoiseSpace.gd: _build_noise, generate_space and inherited collision/mesh creation. Verify the effective noise type and real sampling scale before giving numerical instructions.
evidence: Check visible ground/collider alignment and complete traversal of the proposed route.
Same seed/settings regenerate the same terrain; collider changes match it.
Test steep edges, entry/exit and bounds without claiming universal accessibility.
maps.latitude: Fable may make a mountain refuge, a rolling promenade or another world that carries the body differently. The terrain should invite a route, not become generic noise scenery.
maps.reuse: R4 sample-to-body mapping; R5 arena boundary; R6 local state/seed.

maps.question: What must stay the same before a difference can be attributed to a rule?
maps.body: Two matched fields and the conditions of their comparison.
maps.findings: Both current displays default to simplex-family noise. PerlinNoise.gd and NoiseVisualizer.gd now support a generator config; no Perlin override is placed. The two implementations also vary their sampling and UI. This is a high-value correction before further prose.
build: Set an explicit Perlin basis for the Perlin instance, using the existing configuration path if it reaches the actual generator. Keep the simplex instance explicit too.

Match sample positions, grid size, amplitude, octave count, lacunarity/persistence, animation state and colour mapping. Record seed values; the same integer in different bases means repeatable comparisons, not corresponding features.

Provide reachable common controls plus a selected-coordinate readout. Freeze first and allow one-variable changes. Keep other terrain exhibits secondary; fix the 'Return to Lab' portal's role so the main route clearly continues to Cellular Automata.
book: Begin with a difference the visitor can point to, then ask which cause they have actually isolated.
Repeat each field, vary one shared parameter, and compare again.
Show the exact noise_type selections and shared sampling contract.
Let the names earn their claim. End with the next distinction: sampling a field versus updating a neighbourhood of stored states.
maps.code: PerlinNoise.gd: apply_grid_config/_update_noise_parameters; NoiseVisualizer.gd: _noise_type_for/set_dna/generate_noise_at; SimplexVisualizer.gd setup and sampling.
evidence: Inspect actual runtime noise_type values; assert they differ as labelled.
Check shared parameters and selected coordinate values, plus per-basis replay.
Exercise controls in the museum and verify portal/bypass destination independently of source labels.
maps.latitude: Fable can choose twin reliefs, a shared probe or a reversible display. A fair comparison matters more than preserving the current cabinet.
maps.reuse: R1 controlled comparison; R6 local state/seed; R7 measurement contract.

maps.question: What would you test next if your explanation were still uncertain?
maps.body: A reader choosing a future experiment.
maps.findings: Outside the active museum route. It is a 5×5 reflective exit with a dark sphere and a short existing manuscript. The sphere is currently primary/book-anchored, but it does not itself validate understanding or perform a new noise experiment.
build: Keep this a small, legible pause/return space rather than another instrument-filled lesson.

Offer links or a simple choice of concrete return destinations only through navigation mechanisms the game supports. Test every destination, especially its relation to the main Cellular Automata continuation.
Decide whether the sphere serves a real book encounter or is supporting atmosphere. If reclassified, update roles/anchors together; do not promote decoration just to fill a primary quota.
book: Use a brief recollection of one observed difference instead of summarising every room.
Ask for two possible explanations and the one variable that would distinguish them.
Keep any short code excerpt tied to a previously visited sampler, with a reference; do not manufacture new functionality here.
Leave an attachment or unresolved question with the reader. A 150–250 word coda may be enough; use the length the encounter needs.
maps.code: map_data.json utility definitions and actual portal destination logic; dark_sphere.gd only for behaviours the text genuinely invokes.
evidence: Verify each offered navigation action lands in the named room with a usable return/continuation.
Review book/role treatment after deciding whether the sphere is an encounter.
Confirm no false completion badge, assessment or saved experiment is claimed.
maps.latitude: A bench, an unanswering presence or a small route diagram could work. Preserve the pause; no need to force another manipulation.
maps.reuse: R5 arena boundary; R9 route/book reconciliation.
